relevant_scientific finding: Low-momentum microgravity flames (BRE) can burn for minutes in quiescent atmospheres but self-extinguish in oxygen concentrations below ~25% by volume (methane within 1 minute, larger ethylene flames within 1.5 minutes).
supporting_experimental_evidence: ISS testing using flat porous burners simulating condensed-phase fuels at elevated oxygen concentrations and reduced pressures considered for future spacecraft.
experimental_limitations: Evaluated using gaseous fuel surrogates (methane/ethylene) rather than solid polymers in a constant volume chamber.

application_category: B. Flame spread over solid materials
relevant_scientific finding: Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) research examines extinction behavior and conditions needed for sustained combustion in still atmospheres as a function of material properties.
supporting_experimental_evidence: Simulation of solid/liquid fuel vaporization using flat porous burners matching heats of combustion, gasification, surface temperature, and smoke point.
experimental_limitations: Tested with gaseous fuels in microgravity without forced airflow or actual solid material regression.
